opportunities.funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
opportunities.title: Undergraduate Tuition Fee Grants

amount.raw: grants cover the cost of tuition fees, up to £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Individuals from low-income households, ordinarily resident in Scotland (with at least two years of Scottish secondary/college schooling or a substantial connection to Scotland), enrolled on an undergraduate degree at an eligible Scottish institution, not eligible for government tuition fee funding, and entitled to remain in the UK (or a recognised asylum seeker). Second-degree applicants permitted only in specified subject areas.
opportunities.summary: Grants covering tuition fees for undergraduate students from low-income households who are ineligible for tuition fee support from the Scottish Government, studying at eligible Scottish higher education institutions.

opportunities.funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
opportunities.title: Carnegie-Morgan Scholarship

amount.raw: Full tuition fees for the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants plus an additional living-cost bursary of £1,200

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scottish-domiciled students from low-income households who have been accepted onto the MSc Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants (full-time or part-time) delivered by the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh and the University of Edinburgh; ordinarily resident in Scotland with a Scottish connection; entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK; not previously obtained a postgraduate degree.
opportunities.summary: Scholarship covering full tuition fees plus a £1,200 living-cost bursary for postgraduate study (MSc Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants) at the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh/University of Edinburgh, for students from low-income Scottish households.

opportunities.funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
opportunities.title: Carnegie Masters Grants

amount.raw: Tuition fee payment up to £10,000 (full-time, 1-year) or £5,000 per year (part-time); plus study-cost stipend up to £5,000 (full-time) or £2,500 per year (part-time)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates ordinarily resident in Scotland from low-income households, with a place on an eligible taught or research Masters programme at an eligible Scottish higher education institution, who have applied for the full SAAS postgraduate support package and have not previously completed a postgraduate degree.
opportunities.summary: Grants to help graduates from low-income Scottish households meet the costs of postgraduate (Masters) study at Scottish universities, covering tuition fee top-ups and, in some cases, study-cost stipends. Scheme opens annually 1 May-31 July.
